group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch 2026-09-13: 'Aldaz CM[au]' 138; 'Aldaz CM[au] AND WWOX' 38; 'Nunez MI[au] AND WWOX' 5; 'Ludes-Meyers J[au] AND WWOX' 9.
group_assessment.weighting: Two halves, weighed apart. The group is the laboratory that cloned WWOX (Bednarek 2000a, cited as their own), made the antibody and dominates the early WWOX protein literature — primary for the GENE, and a cancer laboratory, not a group for the neurodevelopmental disease. That authority helps the observation half only partly: this paper is a descriptive histology atlas, not an experiment, and the specificity of the reagent that every call rests on is imported from the group's own earlier papers rather than shown here. The interpretive half — sex-steroid metabolism as the organising principle — is the group's long-standing hypothesis about their own gene, argued from motif and from the tissue list, and it is weighed as the authors' IPOTESI. A stake in the gene's steroid role predicts exactly the error to watch for: organs are grouped by hormonal status in the Discussion while the Discussion's own unweighted 'highest levels' list includes liver, kidney, stomach, salivary gland and neural cells - and of those, stomach is graded only moderate (++) in Results and Table 1, so the list is not a grading. Corrected 2026-09-13 under ALDAZ-REPAIR-B-20260913: the earlier wording called that list the paper's 'strongly positive' list.

queries.query: WWOX AND (normal tissue OR normal tissues)

field_density.note: The CNS cell-type intersections are single-digit. That is what makes this paper's CNS calls — two cores per region, no panel, no co-marker — disproportionately load-bearing for anyone who cites WWOX protein in human astrocytes, ependyma or Purkinje cells. A near-empty intersection is a signal to read the primary, not to trust the citation.

entries.proposition: METHOD: the antibody is a polyclonal raised against the WW-domain region — so it cannot distinguish a WW-domain-bearing product from full-length WWOX on its own, and specificity has to come from somewhere else.
entries.snippet: The antibody was raised against a GST fusion protein harboring the WW domains of the WWOX protein.
entries.anchor: Material and methods, 'Anti-WWOX antibody', sentence 1 (p. 2)
entries.found_or_sought: sought — the compartment question stands or falls on antibody validation

entries.proposition: NEGATIVE FOR THE CORPUS, AND THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: antibody specificity is NOT established in this paper. It is imported from the authors' two 2005 papers, whose control was a WWOX-negative cell-line extract (Peo1). No IHC specificity control — no-primary, preimmune serum, peptide block, or WWOX-null tissue — is described or shown anywhere in this article. PREMISE: INFERENZA resting on unread primaries 15692750 and 15982416 (queued under FT-079).
entries.snippet: We have previously reported on the specificity of the WWOX antibody used for the current study (Nunez et al. 2005a, b), this paper demonstrated specificity by using Peo1 extracts as negative control.
entries.anchor: Material and methods, 'Anti-WWOX antibody', sentence 2 (p. 2)

entries.proposition: Isoform statement is an assertion with a citation: the authors report that only the 46 kDa product is detected as expressed and that they have NO EVIDENCE that other putative alternatively spliced WWOX forms generate stable viable protein products, citing Ludes-Meyers et al. 2003a (Cytogenet Genome Res 100:101-110; the paper does not characterise that reference, and calling it a review is this reader's classification, not the source's word). This is an absence of evidence as the authors state it, not a demonstration that other forms lack stable protein. Two limits on what this paper adds to it: the Methods sentence never cites Fig. 1, and the blot carries only two markers (48 and 29 kDa), which cannot resolve closely spaced products. What the blot does and does not show is entry 36's attestation, not this entry's.
entries.snippet: Only full length WWOX (i.e. the 46 kDa product) is detected as expressed
entries.anchor: Material and methods, 'Anti-WWOX antibody', sentence 3 (pp. 2-3)

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Author's 'no evidence that' had become 'said to lack'; restored as absence of evidence, Fig. 1 limits stated.

entries.proposition: SCORING: a four-level manual scale plus an automated ACIS score 'as previously reported'. No per-organ or per-core values, no n of cores scored per cell type, no inter-observer agreement, no statistics, no statement of how manual and automated grades were reconciled. Nothing is quantified at the level of a cell type.

entries.proposition: SAMPLING DEPTH, in the paper's own terms: combining two serial sections of each TMA gave DUPLICATE REPRESENTATION of 30 organs. The paper gives no number of cores per organ and the TMAs come from three vendors, so what stands behind an organ-level call for those 30 organs is a duplicate representation, not a series - and two serial sections may be the same core cut twice. Breast, ovary, testis and prostate (Methods) and skin (Results) were ADDITIONALLY evaluated on whole tissue sections, with no number of sections stated; ovary and testis were read on TMA cores AS WELL AS whole sections, so the whole-section route supplements the TMA sampling rather than replacing it. The CNS is sampled separately and is entry 7's locator, not this one's.
entries.snippet: by combining two serial sections of each TMA, we obtained duplicate representation of 30 organs
entries.anchor: Material and methods, 'Tissue microarrays and whole tissue sections' (p. 3)

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Scoped the duplicate to the 30 TMA organs in the paper's own words; whole-section organs named as supplementing it.

entries.proposition: CNS NEGATIVES as written in Results: parietal, limbic and temporal cortex and substantia nigra negative; oligodendrocytes negative. Contradicted by the paper's own Table 1 on limbic cortex (entry 12) and softened to +/- for the rest (entry 13).
entries.snippet: Interestingly, the parietal, limbic and temporal cortexes as well as the substantia nigra were negative for anti-WWOX staining. Oligodendrocytes showed no WWOX immunoreactivity.

entries.proposition: Ependymal cells moderately positive; subependymal glia mild; small neurons strong. Text only.
entries.snippet: The ependymal cells from a lateral cerebral ventricle were moderately positive for staining in their scant cytoplasm.
entries.anchor: Results, 'WWOX expression in the nervous system', Brain (p. 6)

entries.proposition: Cerebellum: granule-layer small neurons and molecular layer strong, Purkinje cells MODERATE as written in Results. Table 1 grades the Purkinje layer +++/++ and the molecular layer ++, so the two surfaces rank the layers differently. Text only; no cerebellar panel.
entries.snippet: The folia of cerebellum showed strong positive staining in, small neurons in internal granular cell layer and the molecular layer, while bulbous Purkinje cells stained moderately.
entries.anchor: Results, 'Cerebellum' (p. 6)

entries.proposition: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, UNRESOLVED BY THE PAPER: Table 1 places LIMBIC cortex in the +++ row for neuronal soma and dendrites, while Results (entry 9) calls limbic cortex negative. The two-core sampling (entry 7) makes neither reading checkable, and no panel exists. Verified on the rendered page 16.
entries.snippet: Frontal, occipital, limbic cortex and nucleus caudate: Soma and dendrites of large neurons
entries.anchor: Table 1, Cerebrum, row 1, intensity +++ (p. 16; rendered page16_300dpi-16.png)
entries.found_or_sought: found — by setting the table against the Results sentence

entries.proposition: Table 1 grades parietal cortex, temporal cortex and substantia nigra '+/−', where Results calls them 'negative'. PRINTED FACTS: the Table 1 footnote (p. 17) and Methods define four levels only - negative, mild, moderate, strong - and '+/−' is not one of them; the same text-negative/table-'+/−' pairing occurs for pituitary chromophobic cells (p. 15). THREE READINGS, all available and none defined by the paper: (a) '+/−' marks a borderline call rather than a clean absence; (b) '+/−' is how these authors write the negative they state in prose; (c) '+/−' is a slash RANGE from mild to negative, which is how Table 1 uses its other undefined slash notations ('+++/++', '++/+'). DISAGREEMENT_UNRESOLVED. Note that limbic cortex is NOT in this row: the text calls it negative while Table 1 places it at '+++' (entry 12), a conflict in kind rather than in degree.
entries.snippet: Parietal cortex, temporal cortex and substantia nigra
entries.anchor: Table 1, Cerebrum, last row, intensity +/− (p. 16)

entries.proposition: PANEL QUALIFIES TEXT — the panel says MORE than the text. Fig. 1, five lanes labelled Liver, Kidney, Small Intestine, Heart, Brain: one band just below the 48 kDa marker in EVERY lane — strong in liver and kidney, clearly present at moderate intensity in BRAIN, faint in heart and small intestine; a faint diffuse smear above the band in all lanes. Brain, heart and the very faint small-intestine lane are never mentioned in the running text, which cites Fig. 1 only for liver (lane 1) and kidney (lane 2); the word 'heart' occurs nowhere in the text layer. Loading is NOT equal: the heart actin band is visibly heavier than the others, so the faint heart WWOX band is fainter still per unit loading. Only two markers (48, 29 kDa); no densitometry; no negative-control lane on this membrane. Protein-level detection in whole human brain lysate is therefore a DATO of this figure at single-blot, unquantified strength.

entries.proposition: AUTHOR IPOTESI, not tested here, and quoted at the authors' own strength: they write that the cell-type specificity 'appear[s] to be directly link[ed], at least in part, to the fact that WWOX is an enzyme highly likely to be involved in sex steroid metabolism'. No enzymatic, steroid or receptor measurement exists in the paper; the SDR assignment is by sequence motif (Introduction). The following sentence is a DISJUNCTION - organs 'either steroid targets or related with steroids production/metabolism' - and liver can satisfy its second limb, so a flat counter that the positive organs are not steroid targets in any sense would misread it. What the paper does not do is measure any enzymatic or steroid endpoint, and salivary gland and neural cells are placed by neither limb by any argument it makes. Internal tension in the same argument: the Discussion lists stomach and thyroid among the highest expressers, yet stomach is graded moderate in both Results and Table 1 (++), and thyroid is 'strong' in Results but only ++ in Table 1. PREMISE: DEFAULT_FROM_TEXTBOOK on which organs count as steroid targets or steroid-metabolising.
entries.snippet: Thus, the organs consistently strongly positive, are either steroid targets or related with steroids production/metabolism.
